confirmed.title: Admin PIN lockout is trivially bypassed by rotating anonymous Firebase UIDs
confirmed.detail: The 5-attempt / 15-minute lockout is keyed per user: registerFailedAttempt() and ensureNotRateLimited() both build the rate-limit doc key as sha256(`${uid}:${address}`).slice(...) (lines 61 and 84), where `uid` is the caller's Firebase Auth UID. The app authenticates users with anonymous auth (app.js:520 `signInAnonymously`). An attacker can sign out and call signInAnonymously again before every guess, getting a brand-new UID and therefore a brand-new rate-limit document that starts at failures=0. adminStartSession (lines 395-405) calls ensureNotRateLimited -> compares PIN -> registerFailedAttempt, all keyed on the rotating UID, so the lockout never triggers. The `address` component does not help because a new UID changes the whole key regardless of IP, and clientAddress() (lines 44-48) reads the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header, which is itself spoofable. Net result: unlimited PIN attempts. Against a short numeric PIN (the docs/UX describe a member-entered 'Admin PIN') this is a full offline-speed brute force of admin access, which controls approve/decline/direct-add/cleanup and reading of all private notes.
confirmed.failure: Attacker script loop: signInAnonymously() to get fresh UID, call adminStartSession({pin: guess}); on wrong PIN the failure is recorded under a UID that is never reused, so no request is ever blocked. A 4-6 digit PIN falls in minutes.
confirmed.verifyReason: Verified in functions/index.js: the admin PIN lockout is keyed on sha256(`${uid}:${address}`) (lines 61, 84, 94) where uid is the caller's Firebase Auth UID. The app uses anonymous auth (app.js:520 signInAnonymously) and no App Check is enforced on any onCall (no enforceAppCheck) nor initialized on the client. An attacker can therefore mint unlimited fresh anonymous UIDs (e.g. via the Firebase Auth signupNewUser REST endpoint), each producing a brand-new rate-limit document that starts at failures=0. adminStartSession (lines 396-405) runs ensureNotRateLimited -> PIN compare -> registerFailedAttempt all on that rotating UID, so the 5-attempt/15-minute lockout never triggers. The address component does not help because it is hashed together with the UID, so a changed UID changes the whole key regardless of IP. The PIN input is inputmode='numeric' (app.js:1343), and admin access controls approve/decline/direct-add/cleanup and reading of private booking notes. Correction to the reviewer's framing: this is an online, network-bound brute force (each guess is a callable round-trip), not offline-speed — but the only brute-force defense is still completely defeated, so the defect is real, reachable, and impactful. Correct fix is to key the limiter on client IP alone or add App Check / a global counter rather than the caller-controlled UID.

confirmed.title: `nav` positioning contradicts across generations (sticky top:70 → absolute top:10/right:68), base mobile override also dead
confirmed.detail: Base: `nav { position: sticky; top: 70px; z-index: 29; background: linear-gradient(...); padding: 10px 0 12px; }` (lines 90-94), plus base's own `@media (max-width:520px) { nav { top: 58px; padding-top: 8px; } }` (line 405). v3 gen overrides the base selector to `nav { position: absolute; top: 10px; right: 68px; z-index: 31; padding: 0; background: transparent; }` (line 440), and v3's own mobile query sets `nav { right: 61px; top: 6px; }` (line 490). Because v3's rules come later in the same file with equal specificity, none of the base nav positioning (sticky, top:70/58, gradient fade background, z-index:29) ever renders.
confirmed.failure: The base gen's gradient-fade sticky tab bar and its mobile top:58px tuning are fully inert dead code; z-index also flips (nav 31 > header 30 in v3, vs nav 29 < header 30 in base) meaning the two generations disagree about whether the header or the nav should stack on top — currently nav (containing only the last 2 of 3 tabs, per `.tab:nth-last-child(-n+2)`) floats above the header.
confirmed.verifyReason: Verified by reading the CSS and by rendering the actual page in a browser. Base `nav` rule (lines 90-94: sticky, top:70px, gradient background, z-index:29) and its mobile override (line 405: top:58px) are fully overridden by the later same-specificity `nav` rule at line 440 (position:absolute, top:10px, right:68px, z-index:31, transparent background) and its own mobile override at line 490 — CSS cascade order confirms the base rules are dead code, exactly as claimed. More importantly, this isn't just inert dead code: since v3 also sets `header { position: static }` (line 434), there is no positioned ancestor between `nav` and the viewport, so `nav`'s `position: absolute` places it at 10px from the true page top — overlapping the header's own content instead of sitting below it. Screenshot of the live page confirms visible breakage: the 'My reservations' and 'Live Admin' tab labels render overlapping and illegible in the top-right corner of the header, a real user-facing defect (the primary tab navigation for switching between member/admin views is garbled on load). Category: this is a live functional/legibility bug affecting real users right now, not a stylistic preference for the upcoming rewrite to absorb — recommend fix-now. Severity: high (nav-critical UI element is unreadable), one notch above the reviewer's 'medium'.

confirmed.title: Booking dialog's accessible description is silently blank for the primary open-booking flow
confirmed.detail: bookingModalHtml() builds the aria-describedby text as `esc(needLabel(d.resourceType))` (line 1264). But the draft object created by openBookingFromCell() (lines 1076-1087) — the handler wired to every `data-act="open-booking"` button, i.e. every desktop calendar-cell (line 663), every mobile-resource-btn (line 781), and every availability-slot (line 824) — never sets `d.resourceType` at all; it only sets `d.needs`, `d.preferredRoom`, etc. Only the separate `openMemberDetails()` path (line 1117) sets `resourceType`. `needLabel(undefined)` (line 238-241) returns `undefined`, and `esc(undefined)` (line 100-104) collapses that to `''`.

The dialog's aria-describedby element (id="booking-dialog-summary", read aloud when the dialog receives focus) renders as an empty `` followed by only the time, e.g. " · 2:00pm–2:30pm" — the resource being requested (Study Room / Whiteboard / TV) is never announced or shown, so the user has no confirmation of what they are about to reserve.
confirmed.verifyReason: Verified: openBookingFromCell() (line 1064-1088) is the handler for every data-act="open-booking" trigger (desktop calendar-cell line 663, mobile-resource-btn line 781, availability-slot line 824, dispatched at line 1870). It builds ui.signup with d.needs/d.preferredRoom but never sets d.resourceType. bookingModalHtml() (line 1264) reads esc(needLabel(d.resourceType)); needLabel(undefined) returns undefined (NEED_TYPES.find fails, falls through to returning `type` itself), and esc(undefined) collapses to '' since `undefined == null` is true in JS. Only the separate openMemberDetails() (line 1117) sets resourceType. So the primary booking-open flow renders an empty in the aria-describedby element, meaning screen-reader users get no announcement of which resource (room/whiteboard/TV) they're about to reserve. confirmed.title: Admin PIN brute-force rate limiter is keyed on attacker-controllable anonymous UID
confirmed.detail: registerFailedAttempt/ensureNotRateLimited/clearRateLimit key the counter on `sha256(`${uid}:${address}`)` (lines 61, 84, 94). `uid` is a Firebase anonymous-auth UID (requireAuth only checks request.auth.uid exists). An attacker can call firebase anonymous signIn repeatedly to get a fresh UID, which produces a brand-new rate-limit bucket every 5 attempts, so the MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS=5 / 15-min window (lines 27, 72) never actually blocks. The address is only ever combined WITH the uid into the hash, never used as an independent limit, so it does not help. Combined with the fact that no callable enforces App Check (no enforceAppCheck in functions/), adminStartSession (line 395) is an open endpoint and the Secret-Manager PIN is brute-forceable at unlimited attempt rate; timingSafeTextEqual does not mitigate a guessing attack. A short numeric PIN is fully exposed. Admin access grants approve/decline/direct-add/cleanup and read of privateBookingNotes.
confirmed.failure: Attacker script: loop { anonymous sign-in -> call adminStartSession with next PIN guess }. Each new UID resets the counter, so all 10^4 (4-digit) guesses run without ever hitting the 5-attempt block; admin session token obtained.
confirmed.verifyReason: Confirmed and reachable. The PIN brute-force rate limiter keys its counter on sha256(`${uid}:${address}`) (functions/index.js:61,84,94). requireAuth (line 40) only requires that an anonymous UID exist, and the client signs in via signInAnonymously (app.js:520), so an attacker can mint a fresh UID per attempt. Each new UID produces a new adminRateLimits document, so registerFailedAttempt always computes failures=1 and blocked (1>=5) is never true — the MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS=5/15-min window (lines 27,72) never fires. The client address is only ever hashed together with uid, never used as an independent per-IP limit, so it provides no backstop. adminStartSession (line 395) is an open callable — no enforceAppCheck exists anywhere in the app source (only node_modules references), so nothing prevents scripted calls. timingSafeTextEqual only defeats timing side-channels, not guessing. Given the rate limiter is the design's sole defense (implying a short, human-typed PIN), it is effectively brute-forceable at unlimited rate, granting admin approve/decline/direct-add/cleanup and read of privateBookingNotes. I downgraded the reviewer's 'high' to 'medium' only because the exposed assets are low-value for this small church scheduler (booking management and room notes, no financial/PHI/credential data) and attacker motivation is low — but the security control itself is genuinely broken and should be fixed (enforce App Check, add an IP-independent limit, and lengthen the PIN).

confirmed.title: No rate limit or per-user cap on booking creation lets an anonymous user flood/deface the schedule
confirmed.detail: memberSubmitBooking (lines 183-217, exported line 444) applies no per-user or global rate limit and no cap on how many pending requests one caller may create; requireAuth only checks that some anonymous UID exists. Separately, firestore.rules validMemberCreate (lines 90-116) also permits any signed-in (anonymous) client to write booking documents directly to Firestore, bypassing the callable entirely. Either path lets an attacker create unlimited 'pending' bookings with attacker-controlled `name`/`purposeOther` text across every Tue/Sat slot, wedging the derived waiting line, burying the admin approval queue, and posting arbitrary text on the public board and lobby TV. Anonymous auth means any per-UID mitigation is defeated by UID rotation (app.js:520). The strings are escaped on render (esc() app.js:100-104, escapeHtml() tv.js:59-66, verified applied at every interpolation site) so this is not stored XSS, but it is an unauthenticated spam/DoS/defacement vector on a public-facing board.
confirmed.failure: Attacker loops signInAnonymously + memberSubmitBooking (or direct addDoc under validMemberCreate) to inject hundreds of pending bookings, exhausting all slots and flooding the admin queue with no throttle stopping them.
confirmed.verifyReason: Confirmed real and reachable. memberSubmitBooking (functions/index.js:444, body 183-217) applies no per-user or global rate limit and no cap on pending requests; requireAuth (line 39-42) only checks an anonymous UID exists — and anonymous auth is enabled (app.js:520 signInAnonymously), so UID rotation defeats any per-UID mitigation. Separately, firestore.rules validMemberCreate (lines 90-116) gates only on signedIn(), so an attacker can addDoc directly to /bookings bypassing the callable. Either path lets an unauthenticated caller inject unlimited pending bookings with attacker-controlled name/purposeOther text for the upcoming Tue/Sat dates, flooding the admin approval queue and posting arbitrary text on the public board and lobby TV (tv.js). Output is escaped (esc/escapeHtml verified), so this is spam/DoS/defacement, not XSS. Two reviewer overstatements: pending bookings carry no assignments and only approved bookings conflict (approvedBookingsForDate, line 140), so it cannot literally 'exhaust all slots' to block legitimate approvals, and the damage is reversible via the admin cleanup action. Net: severity medium not high — no data breach, no XSS, reversible, and the target is an obscure small-church link — but it is a genuine unthrottled unauthenticated write vector on both the callable and the security rules, so it warrants a fix (a per-UID/IP throttle plus a pending-count cap; the rules path also needs tightening since schemaVersion mismatch (rules require 3, callable writes 4) shows the direct-write rule is not the intended entry point).

confirmed.title: `.wrap` max-width 1100px (base) dead, overridden to 760px by v3 gen

Identical specificity, v3 wins for max-width and padding-bottom (padding-left/right 16px from base survive since not redeclared). However it's purely a visual/layout defect (alignment/width), not a logic, security, data-integrity, or accessibility-semantics bug, and the file's own comments ('v2 redesign', 'v3 gen') show multiple superseding design passes already layered in this stylesheet, i.e. exactly the kind of leftover cascade cruft a future CSS cleanup would naturally resolve rather than something needing an urgent isolated patch.

confirmed.title: 'My reservations' date selector is decorative — it doesn't filter the list, but looks like it should

Tapping Tuesday or Saturday in this toggle re-renders the exact same combined list of all-dates bookings every time.

confirmed.title: Keyboard focus is not restored after closing the booking modal opened via the member-calendar "Continue" flow
confirmed.detail: closeBookingModal() (lines 1127-1141) restores focus by looking up `ui.returnFocusKey` among elements carrying `data-focus-key`. That key is set in openBookingFromCell() (line 1075: `ui.returnFocusKey = el.dataset.focusKey || ...`) but openMemberDetails() (lines 1111-1125), which is invoked from the `member-continue` button (line 961, wired at line 1869), never sets `ui.returnFocusKey` at all.

confirmed.title: Tab bar uses the ARIA Tabs pattern (role=tablist/tab) but has no keyboard arrow-key navigation, only touch swipe
confirmed.detail: index.html:581 declares `role="tablist"` and app.js:596 renders each tab as `role="tab" aria-selected=...`, which per the WAI-ARIA Tabs authoring pattern implies ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (and Home/End) move selection between tabs. The only directional tab-switching logic that exists in the whole file is `attachSwipeTabs()` (lines 2036-2059), which only listens for `touchstart`/`touchend` — there is no `keydown` handler anywhere for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End (confirmed via grep — zero matches for those key names). Keyboard-only and screen-reader users get a tablist that announces arrow-key semantics but doesn't implement them.
confirmed.failure: A screen-reader user tabs to the tablist, hears "tab, 1 of 3, selected" (standard tablist announcement) and, following convention, presses the Right arrow expecting to move to the next tab — nothing happens. They must instead discover that repeated Tab presses (not arrows) are required, which contradicts the exposed role.

The only tab-switching logic besides direct click is attachSwipeTabs() (app.js:2036-2059), which only wires touchstart/touchend. The single global keydown listener (app.js:2017-2032) is scoped to Escape and Tab-key focus-trapping inside the booking modal (gated on ui.signup) and has nothing to do with the tablist. No ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End handling exists anywhere. This is a real ARIA-pattern mismatch: assistive tech announces standard tablist semantics implying arrow-key nav that isn't implemented. It's not a full keyboard trap (tabs are real <button> elements, so sequential Tab+Enter still reaches and activates each one), so severity is more medium/low than a blocking bug, but it is a genuine semantic-a11y defect worth a small fix (add a keydown handler on the tablist for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End with roving tabindex).

confirmed.title: The live-updating schedule region has no aria-live announcement — only the transient banner strip does
confirmed.detail: `<main id="app" role="tabpanel">` (index.html:585) is where render() (app.js:575-619) rewrites the entire schedule/timeline/chip content every time the Firestore snapshot listener fires (e.g. another member's booking gets approved, cancelled, or a room fills up). Only `#banners` (index.html:584, `aria-live="polite"`) is a live region, and that's populated exclusively by explicit `addBanner()` calls for local action feedback/errors — it is never used to reflect background data changes.

The user's screen reader announces nothing; unless they manually re-navigate the whole grid, they'll act on stale information (e.g. try to book an interval that just became unavailable, only discovering it fails after submitting).

The only live region is #banners (index.html:584, aria-live=\"polite\"), and grepping every addBanner() call site confirms it is invoked exclusively for local action feedback (validation errors, submit confirmations, connection status) — never from the snapshot handler or anywhere reflecting a remote data change. So a screen-reader user watching the schedule gets zero announcement when another member's request is approved/cancelled or a room fills, exactly as claimed. However, given the actual usage pattern of this app (a small church group booking study rooms, not a real-time collaborative tool with frequent concurrent edits), the practical harm is narrow: a user would have to be actively using a screen reader, mid-session, at the exact moment another member's action lands, and then act on stale info before re-reading the grid. That's a real semantic-a11y gap worth fixing, but it's not a severe/blocking defect (no data corruption, and the submit path itself still surfaces a clear error if the slot became unavailable — the DETAIL's failure scenario is real but self-correcting on submit attempt). Rating medium/fix-now: it's a genuine, currently-reachable accessibility gap (not cosmetic, not superseded by an already-planned CSS-only rewrite) and is cheap to fix (add a small aria-live region announcing meaningful diffs, or mark #app polite) — appropriate for fix-now rather than deferral to a visual-only pass.

An attacker can sign out and call signInAnonymously again before every guess, getting a brand-new UID and therefore a brand-new rate-limit document that starts at failures=0. adminStartSession (lines 395-405) calls ensureNotRateLimited -> compares PIN -> registerFailedAttempt, all keyed on the rotating UID, so the lockout never triggers. The `address` component does not help because a new UID changes the whole key regardless of IP, and clientAddress() (lines 44-48) reads the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header, which is itself spoofable. Against a short numeric PIN (the docs/UX describe a member-entered 'Admin PIN') this is a full offline-speed brute force of admin access, which controls approve/decline/direct-add/cleanup and reading of all private notes.

fixNow.title: No rate limit or per-user cap on booking creation lets an anonymous user flood/deface the schedule
fixNow.detail: memberSubmitBooking (lines 183-217, exported line 444) applies no per-user or global rate limit and no cap on how many pending requests one caller may create; requireAuth only checks that some anonymous UID exists. Separately, firestore.rules validMemberCreate (lines 90-116) also permits any signed-in (anonymous) client to write booking documents directly to Firestore, bypassing the callable entirely. Either path lets an attacker create unlimited 'pending' bookings with attacker-controlled `name`/`purposeOther` text across every Tue/Sat slot, wedging the derived waiting line, burying the admin approval queue, and posting arbitrary text on the public board and lobby TV. Anonymous auth means any per-UID mitigation is defeated by UID rotation (app.js:520). The strings are escaped on render (esc() app.js:100-104, escapeHtml() tv.js:59-66, verified applied at every interpolation site) so this is not stored XSS, but it is an unauthenticated spam/DoS/defacement vector on a public-facing board.
fixNow.failure: Attacker loops signInAnonymously + memberSubmitBooking (or direct addDoc under validMemberCreate) to inject hundreds of pending bookings, exhausting all slots and flooding the admin queue with no throttle stopping them.
fixNow.verifyReason: Confirmed real and reachable. memberSubmitBooking (functions/index.js:444, body 183-217) applies no per-user or global rate limit and no cap on pending requests; requireAuth (line 39-42) only checks an anonymous UID exists — and anonymous auth is enabled (app.js:520 signInAnonymously), so UID rotation defeats any per-UID mitigation. Separately, firestore.rules validMemberCreate (lines 90-116) gates only on signedIn(), so an attacker can addDoc directly to /bookings bypassing the callable. Either path lets an unauthenticated caller inject unlimited pending bookings with attacker-controlled name/purposeOther text for the upcoming Tue/Sat dates, flooding the admin approval queue and posting arbitrary text on the public board and lobby TV (tv.js). Output is escaped (esc/escapeHtml verified), so this is spam/DoS/defacement, not XSS. Two reviewer overstatements: pending bookings carry no assignments and only approved bookings conflict (approvedBookingsForDate, line 140), so it cannot literally 'exhaust all slots' to block legitimate approvals, and the damage is reversible via the admin cleanup action. Net: severity medium not high — no data breach, no XSS, reversible, and the target is an obscure small-church link — but it is a genuine unthrottled unauthenticated write vector on both the callable and the security rules, so it warrants a fix (a per-UID/IP throttle plus a pending-count cap; the rules path also needs tightening since schemaVersion mismatch (rules require 3, callable writes 4) shows the direct-write rule is not the intended entry point).

fixNow.title: Tab bar uses the ARIA Tabs pattern (role=tablist/tab) but has no keyboard arrow-key navigation, only touch swipe
fixNow.detail: index.html:581 declares `role="tablist"` and app.js:596 renders each tab as `role="tab" aria-selected=...`, which per the WAI-ARIA Tabs authoring pattern implies ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (and Home/End) move selection between tabs. The only directional tab-switching logic that exists in the whole file is `attachSwipeTabs()` (lines 2036-2059), which only listens for `touchstart`/`touchend` — there is no `keydown` handler anywhere for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End (confirmed via grep — zero matches for those key names). Keyboard-only and screen-reader users get a tablist that announces arrow-key semantics but doesn't implement them.

They must instead discover that repeated Tab presses (not arrows) are required, which contradicts the exposed role.

The only live region is #banners (index.html:584, aria-live=\"polite\"), and grepping every addBanner() call site confirms it is invoked exclusively for local action feedback (validation errors, submit confirmations, connection status) — never from the snapshot handler or anywhere reflecting a remote data change. fixNow.title: selectMemberSlot mutates ui.memberSelection in place BEFORE the full-slot validation, so a rejected range corrupts stored state and bypasses the guard
fixNow.detail: In selectMemberSlot (lines 1097-1108) `selection` is set to the EXISTING ui.memberSelection object when the date/type match, then `tapSlot(selection, ...)` (line 1100) mutates that object's start/end directly (tapSlot does `draft.end = slotEnd`, line 1990). The full-slot check `containsFullTime` is computed AFTER the mutation (lines 1101-1103) and, when it fails, the code `addBanner(...); return;` (lines 1104-1105) WITHOUT calling render() and WITHOUT rolling back. Because `selection === ui.memberSelection`, the extension has already been committed to ui.memberSelection. The only thing skipped is the re-render and the `ui.memberSelection = selection` reassignment (which is now a no-op).
fixNow.failure: Existing selection is 10:00-10:30 (a slot with a free room). Rooms are fully booked 10:30-11:00. User taps 11:00 (an open time) to extend. tapSlot extends ui.memberSelection to 10:00-11:30 in place; containsFullTime detects the full 10:30 slot and shows 'Part of that time is already full' then returns. ui.memberSelection is now the invalid 10:00-11:30 range. On the next render (e.g. an onSnapshot update), the Continue summary shows 10:00-11:30; openMemberDetails passes it to isValidBookingRange (lines 1113/217-223) which only checks window bounds, not occupancy, so it succeeds. The member submits a Saturday request spanning the full 10:30 slot, which is created as a pending in-line booking the guard was meant to prevent.
fixNow.verifyReason: Verified in code: in selectMemberSlot (app.js:1097-1108), when the tap matches the existing selection, `selection` IS `ui.memberSelection`, and tapSlot (app.js:1977-1992, line 1990 `draft.end = slotEnd`) mutates it in place BEFORE the containsFullTime check. On rejection the code does addBanner + return with no rollback and no render (addBanner at 563-571 does not re-render), so ui.memberSelection is left as the invalid extended range. Reachable even without an onSnapshot: the prior render's Continue button is still in the DOM, and clicking it calls openMemberDetails (1111-1113), which only gates on isValidBookingRange (217-223 = window bounds, not occupancy); submitSignup (1286) repeats the same bounds-only check. On a Saturday the backend memberSubmitBooking (functions/index.js:191-195) skips the fully-booked occupancy check (automatic=isTuesday=false) and creates a pending request, so a request spanning a fully-booked 30-min slot IS created. The mutation-without-rollback is a genuine, reachable logic bug and the trivial fix is to mutate a clone or roll back on the reject path. HOWEVER the reviewer overstates impact: this yields only a pending, human-reviewed request, not an assigned/in-line booking, and server integrity still holds — approval (assertNoConflict, functions/index.js:219-221/248-249) and Tuesday auto-assign (193-195) both block any actual double-booking. So no data-integrity breach occurs; the real-world harm is a confusing, un-approvable pending Saturday request that the approver simply can't honor. Real and reachable but low severity, not high.
